subject.title: feat(agents): derive default run concurrency from CPU count

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally change the implicit global agent-run concurrency for existing unconfigured deployments from 4 to a CPU-derived 8–16 range?
rationale: The implementation preserves explicit configuration, but the default governs every existing unconfigured gateway after upgrade and deliberately changes its resource-versus-latency tradeoff.

options.title: Accept the new adaptive default
options.body: Confirm the 8–16 CPU-derived default as the supported upgrade behavior after the branch is rebased and queue behavior is validated on representative host sizes.

options.title: Keep the current default
options.body: Retain 4 for upgrades and pursue a separate opt-in or operator-guided capacity policy if additional parallelism should not be automatic.

recommendation.title: Accept the new adaptive default
recommendation.body: Confirm the 8–16 CPU-derived default as the supported upgrade behavior after the branch is rebased and queue behavior is validated on representative host sizes.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR context identifies steipete as the reporter of the production saturation observation and author of the proposed default-policy change.
